facts.text: A range of Microsoft tools were affected, including the email manager Microsoft Outlook, the workplace messaging and video calling app Microsoft Teams and the A.I. assistant Microsoft Copilot.
By early Friday, Microsoft said that the core functions of Teams and Copilot were online.
Singapore told its taxpayers email capabilities had been disrupted, and the Supreme Court of the Philippines and the European Court of Human Rights said the outage could cause delays in their work.
The global outage affecting Microsoft services reverberated around the world on Friday, upending services relied upon by millions of people.
Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide
Microsoft is investigating a widespread outage affecting multiple Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and Copilot, as users report connectivity problems worldwide.
Microsoft has not yet responded to BleepingComputer's questions about the root cause of the outage and whether it is related to Thursday's earlier Teams disruption.
BleepingComputer has received numerous reports from users experiencing problems accessing Microsoft's services, including complaints that Outlook is down.
Microsoft fixes classic Outlook bug that hid Copilot buttons

"We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure," Microsoft said in its latest update on X.
See what's getting through with a 14-day read-only scan of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, with no MX changes.
The outage follows a separate Microsoft Teams incident earlier Thursday that caused an outage for users in North and South America.
BleepingComputer has also heard from multiple Microsoft Exchange users who report that previously delayed emails have begun trickling into their inboxes as services slowly recover.
The company says the earlier Teams incident has been fully resolved.
Microsoft Outlook to block MSIX attachments starting November

“We appreciate our customer's patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible.” Outage reports on the service uptime tracking website Downdetector began falling around 1:15 pm ET after a large spike in users reporting issues with Outlook and other Microsoft 365 products around noon.
While major Microsoft outages are relatively rare, they are far from unprecedented.

In July 2024, a corrupted update from the security firm CrowdStrike caused the “blues screen of death” on Windows machines around the world, while a separate but nearly simultaneous outage knocked out Microsoft Azure services for hours, causing untold millions of dollars in lost revenue due to companies’ inability to function as normal.
There is currently no indication that a cyberattack caused the current Microsoft outage.

While some apps and features are still running in a degradated state, some people (including Verge staffers) are reporting that access to their emails has been restored, though the flow of Outlook mail might be delayed while efforts to fully fix the outage continue.
Service is gradually starting to recover for Microsoft Outlook and 365 after an almost two-day outage impacting millions of users around the world.

In its latest status page update, dated at 8AM ET on Friday, Microsoft said recovery efforts are going well: > We’re seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements now observed in North America and sustained improvements across much of Europe.
Update, November 13th: Added the latest information from Microsoft.
